evidence.note: run_tests.sh run repeatedly as the outer feedback loop, re-run after each batch of code fixes rather than once — a sustained regular loop, not a one-off pass/fail.

Recurring custom python3 harness invoked with specific LSP method names as arguments (e.g. 'textDocument/documentSymbol textDocument/foldingRange ...'), indicating per-method expected-vs-actual diffing to localize which methods fail beyond the aggregate score.

Inspects the exact Java source file behind failing triples (InlineCalc.java, FlowValid.java, MappingIterator.java, TreeIterator.java) to isolate the divergent case/position — finer localization to single files.
write_stdin calls feed requests directly to the running server, a targeted manual check of individual LSP requests over stdio.

reasoning: The agent drives development with run_tests as the outer loop and layers a reusable per-method diff harness (python3 scripts parameterized by method name) plus per-file source inspection to pinpoint which method and which case diverges, and manually feeds requests over stdio — matching the level-8 description of a tight workflow that diffs per triple, isolates methods/files, and adds targeted manual checks. It stops short of 10 because there is no evidence of engineered regression-guard infrastructure or explicit validation that passes reflect genuine analysis vs. coincidental format matches; re-running the full suite is the only regression mechanism visible.
